body:
@dudynets good point the footer tag does not trigger any rendering specific logic it also has no aria accessibility related features that would help to understand the page

## Conclusion
You can simply not use it as it is up to the developer to not use it and maybe replace it with a custom element like 
```html
<page-end role="note" aria-label="page end reached page loaded">
You Did reach the end of the page. The DOM is also fully loaded at this point so you can interact with it.
</page-end>
</html>
``` 
or similar implementation or even none is a developer choice.

you can maybe start to blog about that but it is not related to the whatwg the history can not be changed the Web Standard has a always stay backward compatible principle but you can influence developers

hope that answers the question and made some sense if so please close. 

As a good influence point i would suggest creating a wordpress plugin that replaces footer with something user configured and write in the plugin description why it exists that way you can easy influence the first people as wordpress has a large userbase many million sites are using it.
